I will keep my land in the wheat-maize cycle this year. In Quzhou County, that is the system I trust most because it fits my water, my labor, and the weather. I want grain that I can sell steadily, and I do not want to gamble on a crop that needs more skill or has a less certain market. So I will stay with winter wheat first, then summer maize on the same land after wheat harvest. For seed, I will use improved wheat and hybrid maize because I want stable emergence, better disease tolerance, and a safer yield. I will not push inputs too hard, but I will feed the crop enough to keep output solid. For wheat, I will plough before sowing, use base fertilizer, then topdress nitrogen around jointing, and irrigate at the key stages because spring drought can cut yield fast. I will spray only when disease, weeds, or aphids are worth controlling. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into maize, keep the turnaround short, use rotary tillage for speed, apply fertilizer in a split way, and irrigate when the rain is not enough, especially around tasseling and grain filling. My goal is not maximum yield at any cost. My goal is a reliable year with manageable work and dependable grain output.
